stories.title: Anthropic sets share price at $83 for stock market debut, above expected range
summary: The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange.The San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set a preliminary share price of $70 to $78 last week.
With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) from $1.26tn to $1.41tn, which would rank it as the second-biggest market offering ever.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX debuted on Wall Street in June with a $1.77tn valuation.

summary: Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year agoPete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

stories.title: US admits ‘substantial’ change to extradition request translation for leftist activist
summary: DoJ cites three examples of alterations from English into Spanish for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers after Guardian reportUS authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish, attributing violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original.Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.
